title: Creating Magic Recipes
description: Learn how to write reusable cooking recipes (functions) that you can perform whenever you want by calling their name!

content.value: Imagine you love baking chocolate cakes. Instead of writing down the 10 steps every time you want a cake, you write them once in a recipe book and name it: 'bake_cake'. Now, whenever you want cake, you just say 'bake_cake()'! In programming, this named recipe is called a Function.
In Python, we define a function using the keyword `def` (which stands for 'define'). We give our function a name, add parentheses `()`, a colon `:`, and then indent the recipe steps underneath.
Defining a function does NOT run it. It just teaches the computer how to do it. To actually perform the function, you have to CALL it by writing its name with parentheses!

def sing_song():
    print("Happy birthday to you!")

# Let's call it twice!
sing_song()
sing_song()
